nodes.name: Alkaline Etching
nodes.procedure: V-NiFe was subjected to etching treatment in a high-concentration KOH solution. Due to the vigorous reaction between the V-NiFe precursor and the strong alkali, partial metal ions dissolved, resulting in the formation of V-doped NiFe-LDH with abundant vacancy defects.

nodes.characterization_summary: XRD patterns match NiFe-LDH (JCPDS No. 40-0215); NiFe-LS shows broader peaks indicating lower crystallinity due to defects.
nodes.evidence_snippet: The X-ray diffraction (XRD) patterns reveal that the diffraction peaks of all prepared samples match well with the crystal planes of NiFe-LDH ... NiFe-LS exhibits broader characteristic diffraction peaks than NiFe-HS, indicating its lower crystallinity

properties.description: X-ray diffraction patterns of various NiFe-based materials

nodes.characterization_summary: NiFe-LS maintains a 2D nanosheet morphology; HRTEM shows a lattice spacing of 0.21 nm for the (018) plane with obvious lattice disorder.
nodes.evidence_snippet: NiFe-LS maintains the original 2D nanosheet morphology ... lattice stripes in NiFe-LS and NiFe-HS is d = 0.21 nm, which closely matches the typical (018) plane ... lattice disorder in the NiFe-LS sample is significantly more obvious

nodes.characterization_summary: Fe 2p peaks at 711.5 and 724.5 eV confirm Fe3+; Ni 2p shows a slight negative shift for NiFe-LS. Fe 3s multiplet splitting (4.7 eV) confirms LS/IS Fe3+.
nodes.evidence_snippet: Fe 2p XPS spectrum of NiFe-LS shows two peaks at 711.5 and 724.5 eV ... multiplet energy separation values (delta E3s) of Fe 3s double peaks for NiFe-LS and NiFe-HS are 4.7 and 6.1 eV

features: First shell peak at ~1.6 Å (likely M-O/N coordination)
Second shell peak at ~2.8 Å (likely M-M coordination)

nodes.characterization_summary: EXAFS shows lower coordination numbers for Fe-O (4.4) and Ni-O in NiFe-LS compared to NiFe-HS (5.3), confirming high-density vacancy defects.
nodes.evidence_snippet: coordination number (CN) of Fe—O and Fe—Fe/Ni scattering for NiFe-LS is 4.4 and 4.3 ... significantly lower than those of NiFe-HS (5.3 and 5.1)

nodes.characterization_summary: EPR confirms a transition from high-spin Fe3+ in NiFe-HS to predominantly low-spin Fe3+ in NiFe-LS.
nodes.evidence_snippet: NiFe-HS exhibits a prominent signal corresponding to high-spin Fe3+ , whereas NiFe-LS displays a distinct signal attributing to low-spin Fe3+

nodes.characterization_summary: NiFe-LS exhibits paramagnetic behavior with a lower effective magnetic moment (3.6 mu_B) than NiFe-HS (4.5 mu_B).
nodes.evidence_snippet: NiFe-LS exhibits a linear magnetic hysteresis curve, which corresponds to the paramagnetic behavior ... value for NiFe-LS (3.6 mu_B) is lower than that of NiFe-HS (4.5 mu_B)
